title: I Took the Astronomy-Club Dobsonian Checkout to the Intern Who Skipped the Collimation Log

parts.text: I rolled dob three to the pad at 8:11 p.m. and intern Kade was already viewing through our numbered focuser. The card said: ONE SCOPE. TWO HOURS. COLLIMATE AND LOG. I was forty-two, club lead, holding a star chart that listed our target. Kade shrugged. "Interns are the sky." I photographed the card, the log, and his eyepiece in our focuser. Then I asked for the collimation sheet. At 8:19 the pad pinged why Kade's name was not on our dob. I kept my voice dark-adapted and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The pad can see Kade's eyepiece in our focuser during our checkout.

social.video_title: He viewed through our numbered focuser without the log — Part 1/2
social.description: Dobsonian pad, an intern in our focuser, a collimation log he skipped. I logged the eyepiece. Would you have asked for the sheet?

parts.text: Kade called it a peek until the pad asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the eyepiece still. The focuser went back to our cap. Kade ran his own two hours and told the next intern atmosphere was always about seeing. Seeing is a word interns use when a log exists. Scope policy now has a second line: INTERNS ARE NOT THE SKY. I keep our dob on a labeled dolly. Kade brown-bags his jokes. The pad finally looks like a checkout, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Collimation sheet, numbered focuser, and a second line on the card. Was a peek ever our dob?
